games.name: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2021 results name Animal Crossing: New Horizons as the Game Beyond Entertainment winner; it also won Multiplayer.

mechanics.name: real-time island routine
mechanics.detail: Seasons and time of day track real life; fishing, bugs, fossils, gardening and collecting rotate the daily activity set.

mechanics.name: resident and island development
mechanics.detail: Players decorate and improve an island while meeting animal residents and using Nook Miles for goals and unlocks.

games.return_reason: Calendar novelty, collection completion, decorating, and resident/social events create low-pressure daily return reasons. This is a loop inference, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Use city calendars, resident visits, collectible/career goals, and visible home/public-space customization to make a human-life city feel alive between missions.
games.risk: Daily chores can become obligation and shallow checklist play; resident simulation may be expensive to author.

games.name: Stardew Valley

award.name: PlayStation.Blog Game of the Year 2016 reader poll

games.award_evidence: PlayStation.Blog records Stardew Valley as Bronze in its reader poll; Firewatch received the Platinum first-place award.

mechanics.name: farm economy
mechanics.detail: The farm and shared money drive progression; players grow, craft and reinvest over repeated in-game days.

mechanics.name: relationships and festivals
mechanics.detail: Villagers have friendship progression, gifts and scheduled festivals that alter social opportunities and rewards.

mechanics.name: co-op persistence
mechanics.detail: Multiplayer shares the farm, money and world progress while inventories, skills and relationships remain player-specific.

games.return_reason: The day/season clock, farm compounding, NPC schedules, festivals and bundles make each session feed the next. Inference only; no retention metric claimed.
games.allworld_transfer: Model resident careers and businesses as seasonal projects, with festivals and relationship milestones producing shared city consequences.
games.risk: Clock pressure and repetitive chores can punish casual players; authored NPC schedules require consistency.
games.retention_type: seasonal progression + relationship routine + cooperative world persistence

games.name: Minecraft
games.award_evidence: The official 2011 Game Developers Choice Awards record names Minecraft as Best Debut Game.

mechanics.name: resource-to-build loop
mechanics.detail: Players gather resources, craft tools, build shelters and engineer bases in an infinite world.

mechanics.name: mode choice
mechanics.detail: Survival adds hostile mobs and resource pressure; Creative supplies unlimited resources, flight and immunity.

mechanics.name: persistent multiplayer
mechanics.detail: Realms and servers provide persistent shared worlds, cross-play and community-made activities.

games.return_reason: Open-ended projects, emergent discovery and persistent shared worlds create self-directed reasons to return. This is design inference, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Give residents and players persistent places to build, repair and personalize, with city-scale projects that create visible history and social coordination.
games.risk: Extreme openness can weaken authored missions and overwhelm first-time players; simulation/build state can be costly to stream.
games.retention_type: self-directed creation + exploration + persistent social world

games.name: The Sims
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2000 category page names The Sims as Game of the Year.
games.edition_note: The award belongs to the original 2000 game. The cited 25th-anniversary Legacy Collection page is a modern re-release page that explicitly carries the original game's core design forward.

mechanics.name: direct life control
mechanics.detail: EA's modern Legacy Collection page describes the re-released original game as creating Sims and homes, then guiding careers, friendships and romance or allowing chaos.

mechanics.name: household storytelling
mechanics.detail: EA's modern Legacy Collection page preserves the original household-and-home framing through personality and skill creation, home building and open-ended life guidance.

games.return_reason: Stories emerge from interacting needs, relationships, work and home design; players return to continue a household narrative or test a new one. Inference, not retention measurement.
games.allworld_transfer: Make each AI resident legible through needs, aspirations, work, relationships and a home that changes with choices, while allowing player-directed intervention.
games.risk: Highly combinatorial simulation can produce brittle behavior and ethical discomfort if resident agency is cosmetic.
games.retention_type: emergent narrative + household progression + creative authorship

games.name: The Sims 2
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2005 category page names The Sims 2 as Simulation Game of the Year.
games.edition_note: The award belongs to the original 2004 game. The cited 25th-anniversary Legacy Collection page is a modern re-release page that explicitly carries the original game's life-stage and generational design forward.

mechanics.name: life-stage simulation
mechanics.detail: EA's modern Legacy Collection page describes the re-released original game as guiding Sims across whole lives, with traits and choices carried across generations.

mechanics.name: multi-generational continuity
mechanics.detail: EA's modern Legacy Collection page explicitly describes evolving a family tree across multiple generations while building homes and neighborhoods.

games.return_reason: Generational change and household continuity create a longer arc than a single scenario; players return to see consequences and build new family stories. Inference only.
games.allworld_transfer: Persist resident memories, family ties, home ownership and career effects so city stories survive beyond one mission or avatar session.
games.risk: Continuity creates save-state complexity and can expose weak AI if relationships or life transitions do not make sense.

games.name: Sid Meier's Civilization IV
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2006 category page names Civilization IV as Strategy Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: resource and state management
mechanics.detail: The award category describes strategy play as directing resources to create conditions for success through planning rather than execution.

games.return_reason: The turn structure makes every choice feed a longer strategic arc, while alternate civilizations and maps support replay. Inference, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Represent city policy, infrastructure, careers and diplomacy as compounding systems with several viable success conditions.
games.risk: Macro systems can flatten individual residents into statistics and make onboarding opaque.

games.name: Sid Meier's Civilization V
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's Strategy archive marks Civilization V as the 2011 winner.

mechanics.name: resource-directed strategy
mechanics.detail: The strategy category defines the core loop as manipulating resources to create winning conditions through planning rather than execution.

games.return_reason: Persistent world state, competing objectives and alternate leaders create a replayable planning loop. This is an inference, not a retention claim.
games.allworld_transfer: Let city policies, residents, employers and districts create second-order effects that make each mission alter the next civic decision.
games.risk: Systemic depth can obscure human-scale stories and create runaway leaders.

games.name: Sid Meier's Civilization VI
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 20th D.I.C.E. results name Civilization VI as Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: resource and victory planning
mechanics.detail: The award category describes strategy as directing resources to create success conditions, emphasizing planning over execution.

mechanics.name: evolving civilization state
mechanics.detail: Cities, technologies, districts, diplomacy and culture create a changing empire state over many turns.

games.return_reason: District-style specialization and multiple victory routes make the same map support different strategic identities. Inference only; no retention metric.
games.allworld_transfer: Give neighborhoods, employers and resident groups distinct development paths so players can shape a city through trade-offs rather than a single upgrade tree.
games.risk: High systemic interdependence can be difficult to communicate and tune for a life-world audience.

games.name: Age of Empires IV
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 25th D.I.C.E. winners page names Age of Empires IV as Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: economy-to-army loop
mechanics.detail: Players explore, gather food/wood/gold/stone, build structures, train units and advance through Ages.

mechanics.name: multiple victory conditions
mechanics.detail: Landmark, Sacred and Wonder victories create distinct strategic goals and end states.

mechanics.name: campaign and multiplayer modes
mechanics.detail: Four historical campaigns coexist with skirmish, cooperative AI and competitive multiplayer.

games.return_reason: Fast resource decisions, civilization asymmetry and multiple victory paths generate replayable matches and campaign mastery. Inference only.
games.allworld_transfer: Use districts and resident factions with different economies and missions, while offering civic, cultural and economic ways to win a city chapter.
games.risk: Real-time pressure may conflict with reflective life-sim play and accessibility goals.
games.retention_type: match replay + mastery + asymmetric campaign identity

games.name: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2011 category page names StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty as Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: resource and unit production
mechanics.detail: Players use economy, tech and unit composition to create tactical answers in real-time battles.

mechanics.name: persistent online competition
mechanics.detail: The title won AIAS awards for both strategy/simulation and online gameplay, reflecting ranked and social replay structure.

games.return_reason: A strong campaign arc pairs with repeatable competitive matches and build-order mastery. This is return-loop analysis, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Offer residents and organizations distinct capabilities, readable counters and missions whose outcomes depend on preparation and adaptation.
games.risk: Competitive optimization may crowd out believable social behavior and create steep onboarding.
games.retention_type: skill mastery + competitive replay + campaign progression

games.name: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos

award.name: 6th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards
award.category: Computer Strategy Game of the Year

games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2003 game record identifies Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos as Computer Strategy Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: race-based RTS
mechanics.detail: Players command four races, build armies and seize objectives through real-time resource and combat decisions.

mechanics.name: hero-led campaign
mechanics.detail: The campaign centers pivotal story events around heroes, factions and more than 60 missions in the modern re-creation.

games.return_reason: Hero progression gives a personal anchor to macro strategy while faction campaigns create narrative momentum. Inference, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Anchor city strategy in named resident leaders whose careers, loyalties and personal missions change how districts function.
games.risk: Hero-centric design can over-centralize agency and reduce the wider resident population to backdrop.

games.name: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle

award.name: Game Critics Awards: Best of E3 2017

games.award_evidence: Ubisoft's official report says Kingdom Battle won Best Strategy Game at the Game Critics Awards' Best of E3 2017; this was pre-release recognition.

mechanics.name: turn-based cover tactics
mechanics.detail: Teams use movement, cover, dashes, team jumps and weapons on tactical battlefields.

mechanics.name: mission variety and upgrades
mechanics.detail: Campaign battles use changing objectives and unlock stronger weapons and abilities between encounters.

games.return_reason: Readable tactical rules, character synergies and changing objectives make short sessions satisfying while preserving campaign progression. Inference only.
games.allworld_transfer: Translate city missions into compact tactical situations where resident skills, terrain and relationships combine to solve local problems.
games.risk: Puzzle-like missions may feel disconnected from persistent residents unless outcomes carry into the city state.
games.retention_type: short-session mastery + team synergy + campaign unlocks

games.name: Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope
games.award_evidence: Ubisoft's FY23 Q3 release states that Sparks of Hope won Best Sim/Strategy Game at The Game Awards 2022.

mechanics.name: open-world planets
mechanics.detail: Players explore planets with inhabitants, puzzles, side quests and optional enemies outside self-contained battlefields.

mechanics.name: free-movement turn combat
mechanics.detail: Heroes move within a radius, use cover, team jumps and abilities, and combine Sparks for tactical synergies.

mechanics.name: skill progression
mechanics.detail: Skill trees and level-earned Skill Prisms let players specialize heroes for different team roles.

games.return_reason: Exploration, side quests, flexible team builds and reshuffled battlefields create both discovery and mastery returns. Inference only.
games.allworld_transfer: Separate city exploration from instanced missions, then carry resident relationships, skill builds and local discoveries between them.
games.risk: Large authored worlds can dilute resident simulation and produce content volume pressure.

games.name: Fire Emblem: Three Houses
games.award_evidence: The Game Awards' 2019 edition archive names Fire Emblem: Three Houses as Best Strategy Game.

mechanics.name: academy time management
mechanics.detail: Players choose a house and spend free time exploring the monastery, teaching students, battling, taking exams, seminars or resting.

mechanics.name: relationship-linked tactics
mechanics.detail: Grid battles, paired units and support relationships increase combat options and Gambit effects.

games.return_reason: The monthly calendar makes social investment and combat preparation compete for scarce time, with house paths encouraging repeat campaigns. Inference, not retention data.
games.allworld_transfer: Use a city calendar where residents learn, work, socialize and take missions; relationships should change team capability and narrative access.
games.risk: Time-boxed social optimization can become repetitive busywork and may make residents feel like stat bundles.
games.retention_type: calendar planning + relationship progression + branching replay

games.name: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2013 category page names XCOM: Enemy Unknown as Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: soldier permadeath and abilities
mechanics.detail: Soldier classes have unique abilities; loss and survival alter the squad’s future strength.

mechanics.name: base, research and engineering
mechanics.detail: The headquarters view manages facilities, research and development, turning strategic choices into tactical capability.

games.return_reason: Permanent consequences, escalating threats and a strategic/tactical split create strong comeback and mastery loops. This is inference, not measured retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Make resident injuries, career failure and city infrastructure damage persist, so mission choices create emotionally legible stakes and preparation needs.
games.risk: Punishing failure can frustrate a broad life-world audience; persistent casualties need careful consent and tone.
games.retention_type: high-stakes consequence + preparation mastery + campaign recovery

games.name: Into the Breach
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2019 game record identifies Into the Breach as Strategy/Simulation Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: telegraphed tactical puzzles
mechanics.detail: Enemy attacks are readable, and mech pushes or attacks can redirect threats away from civilian buildings.

mechanics.name: island objectives and resets
mechanics.detail: Runs defend islands and objectives; failed timelines send the team back through time with selected progression.

games.return_reason: Short, information-rich turns reward experimentation, while resets turn failure into another attempt with retained knowledge. Inference only.
games.allworld_transfer: Design city missions around readable resident needs and preventable consequences, with safe retries that preserve learning and selected civic progress.
games.risk: Puzzle determinism may feel too abstract for open-ended human stories; resets can weaken consequence if overused.
games.retention_type: short-session mastery + reversible failure + roguelite replay
